intro.caption: Lesson 3-10 — convert measurement units. Race day! Track sensors report in yards, kilograms, and gallons, but Omar's headline screen needs inches, grams, and cups.

balloons.t: Stop the presses! The jump ramp is 6 yards, and my headline needs INCHES!
Don't skip a unit in the chain! Convert yards to feet, then feet to inches.
6 yards times 12 is 72 inches! Headline ready: Zara jumped 72 inches!
72 inches is six FEET, Omar! You skipped yards-to-feet completely!

pages.caption: Skipping a link in a multi-step conversion turns yards into feet instead of inches. Chain every conversion factor so each unwanted unit cancels.

balloons.t: Line up the conversion steps in order so each old unit cancels out cleanly.
Write each conversion factor, multiply or divide in order, and check the final unit.
Customary or metric—never jump over the middle unit!
Wait—my draft says 2.5 kilometers is 250 meters! Did I miss a zero?
Check the factor before you hit publish! One kilometer is 1,000 meters.
Three final stats to convert before the front page goes live!
The headline is live, every unit is right, and I still have time for lunch!

win.caption: Multi-step conversions chain one conversion factor after another until the target unit is left. Check every step so no unit gets skipped.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Choose the Chain
gates.prompt: Put the conversion steps in order to turn yards into inches, then compute the jump distance.
hints: Conceptual: each step trades the current unit for the next one until you reach inches.
Procedural: start with yards, multiply by 3 ft / 1 yd to cancel yards, then multiply by 12 in / 1 ft to cancel feet.

worked.q: How many inches are in 3 yards?

items.q: Tap the steps in order to convert 6 yards into inches:
items.fb: Start with yards, convert yards to feet first (× 3), then convert feet to inches (× 12).

items.label: 6 yards = ___ inches (1 yd = 3 ft, 1 ft = 12 in)

fb.msg: 72 is 6 × 12—that skipped converting yards to feet first!
18 is 6 yards in FEET. Now multiply 18 feet by 12 inches per foot.

gates.pass: 216 inches! That's a real headline jump—not 72 inches!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Convert Without Skipping
gates.prompt: Convert two more race-day stats without skipping a step.
hints: Conceptual: check whether the target unit is smaller (multiply) or larger (divide) at each step.
Procedural: 1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 2 pints; 1 m = 100 cm and 1 km = 1,000 m.

steps: Practice: convert 2 gallons to pints (1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 2 pt).

items.label: 5 gallons of fuel = ___ pints (1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 2 pt)

fb.msg: 20 is 5 gallons in QUARTS. Convert quarts to pints (× 2).
10 is 5 × 2—that skipped the 4 quarts per gallon step.
Meters are larger than centimeters, so divide 450 by 100 instead of multiplying.
1 meter is 100 cm, not 10 cm. Divide 450 by 100.

gates.pass: 40 pints of fuel and 4.5 meters! Every unit canceled cleanly.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Fix the Headline
gates.prompt: Catch the conversion error in Omar's draft before it hits the front page.
hints: Conceptual: check the conversion factor and decimal place value.
Procedural: 1 km = 1,000 m, so multiplying by 1,000 shifts the decimal point three places right.

steps: Practice: convert 1.5 km to meters (1 km = 1,000 m).

items.q: Omar wrote: "2.5 km = 250 m." What went wrong?

options.t: He multiplied by 100 instead of 1,000; 2.5 km is 2,500 m

options.fb: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiplying is right—just use 1,000, not 100.
Unit conversions multiply or divide by the factor, never add.

options.t: Nothing went wrong; 2.5 km is 250 m
options.fb: 1 km = 1,000 m, so 2 km is already 2,000 m.

fb.msg: That multiplies by 100. Use 1,000 meters per kilometer.
2.5 × 1,000 shifts the decimal three places right: 2,500, not 25,000.

gates.pass: 2,500 meters! Omar's draft is saved from a front-page typo!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Press Deadline
gates.prompt: Three final conversions before the Race Day Report goes live.
hints: Conceptual: put measurements in the same unit before comparing, and never skip a link in a multi-step chain.
Procedural: use 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 lb = 16 oz, and 1 ft = 12 in.

steps: Practice: compare 4 lb and 70 oz (1 lb = 16 oz).
70 oz > 64 oz, so 70 oz is heavier.
worked.q: How many ounces are in 3 pounds?

items.label: Lock 1 · A trophy has mass 1.8 kg. How many grams? (1 kg = 1,000 g)
Lock 2 · 2 yards and 1 foot = ___ inches total (1 yd = 3 ft, 1 ft = 12 in)
items.aria: 2 yards and 1 foot converted to total inches

fb.msg: 72 inches is 2 yards (6 feet). Do not forget the extra 1 foot (12 inches)!
Convert both yards and feet: 2 yd = 6 ft, plus 1 ft = 7 ft total, then × 12.

items.fbDefault: Turn 2 yards into 6 feet, add 1 foot to get 7 feet, then multiply by 12.

items.q: Lock 3 · Zara's crate is 5 pounds. Rival's crate is 76 ounces (1 lb = 16 oz). Which headline is true?

options.t: Zara's crate is heavier (80 oz > 76 oz)

options.fb: You cannot compare 5 pounds and 76 ounces without converting to the same unit.

options.t: Both crates weigh the exact same
options.fb: 5 lb × 16 = 80 oz, which is more than 76 oz.

gates.pass: PRINT IT! 1,800 g, 84 inches, and 80 oz > 76 oz—the Race Day Report hits the stands!

journal.heading: Lesson 3-10 — what the press desk taught us
rows: Arrange conversion factors so the unit you are leaving cancels out and only the target unit remains.
Never skip a middle unit (like feet between yards and inches). Multiply or divide step by step.
In metric, 1 km = 1,000 m and 1 kg = 1,000 g—shift the decimal three places, not two.
Convert mixed units (like pounds and ounces) into the same unit before writing a comparison.
journal.quote: "Six yards is 216 inches, not 72. Always check the middle step before you hit publish!" — Omar

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-10 (Convert Measurement Units). Covers multi-step unit conversions, canceling units cleanly, avoiding skipped steps, and comparing measurements in different units.
standards: Use ratio reasoning and conversion factors to convert measurement units
